title: Feature-fence policy lattice for graceful upgrades and staged rollback
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Implement a policy-driven "feature-fence" lattice that coordinates percent-ramps, flag scoping, and automated rollback decisions to reduce upgrade risk for runtime and model-serving changes. The lattice composes multiple orthogonal gates (latency, error-rate, correctness/regression checks, cold-start anomalies, and cost spikes) into an ordered policy graph. Each gate emits stability credits and can escalate to a fence (block traffic expansion) or trigger an automated rollback with an explainable score.

Rationale: Existing canary and staged-rollout tooling focuses on simple static ramps or single-metric triggers. High-risk upgrades need composable checks so we can: (1) allow safe partial exposure by region/tenant, (2) delay expansion while background verification runs, and (3) make rollback decisions that balance signal quality and customer impact. The "feature-fence" concept is a lightweight guardrail that can be attached to routes, model-variants, or tenant cohorts via a single API and UI surface.

Scope: 
- Orchestrator: policy lattice evaluation engine in the control plane (expressed as ordered gates with thresholds and hysteresis).
- Flagging: feature-fence ties to existing feature flag system; supports scoped flags (tenant, org, region) and percent-based splits.
- Metrics & telemetry: new rollout-health composite metric (stability_score) and per-gate diagnostics; integrates with Console and Grafana dashboards.
- Rollback scorer: deterministic scoring function that combines gate signals into a rollback decision and rationale.
- Simulation: offline rollout simulator for testing policies against historical traffic.

Out of scope for this ticket: on-prem private control plane changes (will be tracked separately), and long-term ML-based anomaly detection (future enhancement).
acceptance_criteria: Policy lattice can be defined via JSON/YAML and persisted to control plane
Feature-fence can be attached to a route or model variant and scoped to tenant/region
Percent ramps respect active fences and will pause/attenuate automatically when fence conditions breach
Rollback scorer produces an explainable decision and triggers automated rollback when policy-declared thresholds are exceeded
Console shows per-gate health and a composite stability_score for any active rollout
Simulator can replay a 7-day traffic window and surface policy violations with per-gate timelines
steps: Design: finalize gate taxonomy and scoring model (latency, errors, semantic-regression, cold-start, cost)
API: implement lattice spec and attach points for flags/routes
Control plane: evaluate lattice on incoming telemetry and emit stability_score
Console: add rollout inspector panel and per-gate timelines
E2E: run staged rollout against canary fleet, validate automated pause/rollback behavior
Docs: publish runbook and policy examples for SREs and product owners
comments: 2025-02-12 Aisha Kapoor: Initial ticket created. Captured high-level design and goals after sync with PM and SRE. Marked P1 due to recent incidents during model variant upgrades.

2025-02-18 Marco Li: Spike completed for lattice evaluation engine. Prototype uses weighted gates and exponential backoff when gating expands. Findings: need guard against metric flapping; plan to add hysteresis windows.
2025-02-24 Design review: UX team suggested 'explainable rollback' UI and a lightweight 'why did we pause?' view. Added links to example flows in design doc.
2025-02-28 Engineering: implemented API v1 for fence spec; scaffolded evaluator but not yet wired to telemetry ingestion. Created PR #12890.
2025-03-03 QA: simulator run against last 30 days of production traffic shows 12 false pauses due to short-lived spike; adjust gate windowing from 1m to 5m and add stability credits for warm starts.
2025-03-04 Marco Li: Updated acceptance criteria and schedule. Next: integrate Console panel and run full canary with traffic shadow for two weeks.
notes: Trade-offs considered: simpler single-metric rollbacks are easier to reason about but produce noisy rollbacks; multi-gate lattice reduces noise but increases complexity and operator cognitive load.
Operational playbook: default policy will be conservative (slower ramps, lower max burst) for tenant cohorts with high SLA requirements. Non-critical tenants will use aggressive default.
Fallback: when control plane is degraded, fences default to 'allow with monitoring' to avoid broad customer impact; this behavior is configurable per-policy.
Related: will coordinate with the Dedicated autoscaling team to ensure fences can interact with capacity-based routing changes.
